clue.text: See a' drug act so badly, they stop running

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of these words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An onlooker winces at a drug-taking performance so poor that it ends with people fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' here is smuggling (running contraband ashore), which the shore patrol exists to stop; 'See' merely invites the solver to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Running means smuggling goods ashore, and the shore patrol service exists to stop smugglers.

clue.text: Lightweight ,article written in awkward situation?

indicators.note: written in means the article is placed inside the other word

parts.note: 'in the cart' is British slang for in trouble or an awkward situation

explanation.surface: A trivial piece written about an embarrassing predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the cart' is British slang for being in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is a tiny unit of weight for gems, 200 milligrams.

clue.text: Unusual in a bar, isn't 'e?

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are arranged out of their normal order

parts.note: the letters of isn't, without the apostrophe
'e is a dropped-aitch he, giving its letter E

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a man who seems out of place in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; the whole clue is also the definition, since a teetotaller in a pub is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller who refuses alcohol would be an oddity among drinkers in a pub.

clue.text: Master's skill seen in next school tune, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests this is one possible rearrangement of the words

parts.note: the fodder as the setter meant it, with THEN in place of NEXT

explanation.surface: A headmaster's flair is shown in the new school song.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signalled by 'perhaps' works only if 'next' is read as 'then': the printed X must be H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nelson touch is a phrase for the brilliant leadership flair shown by Admiral Nelson, a master mariner.

clue.text: Lacking form before first test

explanation.surface: A pupil short of ability before the first examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' is a racing word: a horse's record of past results, which a debutant lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A racehorse yet to run has no form record; anything not yet tried out has had no trial, so both senses mean untested.

clue.text: Is it beneath a clergyman to call again?

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath means the words that follow come after the clergyman

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A question of whether a minister is above making return visits.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back and visit once more is to call again.

clue.text: Composer cut short vacation

indicators.note: cut short means the composer's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Gustav Holst, composer of The Planets

explanation.surface: A composer's holiday is curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hols is British informal shortening of holidays, a break from school or work.

clue.text: Sort of bulb one planted in small numbers coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from the bottom upwards
planted in means one letter is set inside the others

parts.note: no. is a short form of number, so two of them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gardener plants one bulb among a few that are sprouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted in' puts I into NONO, making NOINO, and 'coming up' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion grows from a bulb and is a kind of bulb vegetable.

clue.text: Cheese that needs to mature in Southern city

indicators.note: in means the word for mature is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: Derby is a city in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A cheese that must be ripened in a southern city.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is a city in England's East Midlands; the cheese is flavoured with sage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage Derby is an English hard cheese marbled green with sage.

clue.text: Novel way to abridge classic work

explanation.surface: A fresh method of shortening a great book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' is a noun, not 'new'; the second sense is Gibbon's history, The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh's first novel; also the short form of Gibbon's great Roman history title.

clue.text: A particular honour

explanation.surface: A particular honour bestowed on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: In this regard one may say 'in every particular' or 'in every way'; to honour someone is to hold them in esteem.

clue.text: Contemplating how to struggle forward

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
a wing is a forward position in football and rugby

explanation.surface: Someone ponders how best to press on through difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like a direction but is a player: a winger in football or rugby plays up front.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at something attentively is a form of contemplating it.

clue.text: Hears about old disasters

indicators.note: about means the word for hears goes around the word for old

parts.note: a judge tries, or hears, a case

explanation.surface: Someone listens to tales of past calamities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hears' is the court sense: a judge hears, or tries, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Great calamities or catastrophes are commonly called tragedies.

clue.text: Defensive position Duke reinforced

explanation.surface: A duke's defences are strengthened.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment or wall given an inner layer is lined, which strengthens or backs it.

clue.text: Secret Service chief visiting America less

parts.note: M is the head of the Secret Service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: The spy chief is on a trip to the United States, with something missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten less two is ten take away two: subtraction is said both ways.

clue.text: Mistakenly, some let it become an excuse for smacking

indicators.note: mistakenly suggests the words are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly lets a thing become a pretext for hitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smacking' is smacking the lips, a kiss, as under the Christmas plant, not a slap.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing under the hanging sprig at Christmas is a custom, so it gives an excuse for a kiss.

clue.text: Register recorded reject explosive device

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the two words found are written backwards as one run

parts.note: a rota is a register or roster of duties

explanation.surface: Officials log and then refuse a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reject' turns the whole run ROTANOTED backwards, giving DETONATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A small charge used to set off a bigger explosive is a detonator.

clue.text: Acerbic leaders in Times really delight

indicators.note: leaders means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The newspaper's leading articles are sharp and witty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' is not editorials here but the opening letters of 'Times' and 'really'.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting, incisive comment is acerbic and sharp.

clue.text: Player trying to win a hand

definitions.text: Player trying to win a hand

parts.words: Player trying to win a hand
parts.note: a hand here is a hand in marriage, not cards, and the player is a musician singing beneath a window to woo

explanation.surface: A card player hopes to take the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor who sings or plays under a lady's window to woo her, hoping for her hand in marriage.

clue.text: Temptress cheered up, having pocketed money

indicators.note: having pocketed means the reversed word takes the money inside it
in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds, money

explanation.surface: A seductress grows happier after taking cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses HAILED to DELIAH, which takes L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Delilah seduced Samson in the Bible, and her name is used for any seductress.

clue.text: Sound of row with lunatic of Latin origin

indicators.note: sound of means we hear the word for row pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: row in the rowing sense rhymes with go

explanation.surface: A loud quarrel with a madman of Roman descent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' must be pronounced like 'go', not as a quarrel, to give the sound RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Romanic describes languages derived from the Latin of Rome.

clue.text: Imitative behaviour seen in animal house

explanation.surface: Copycat conduct is seen at the zoo's primate enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Aping is mimicry, so copying others is aping; a place where apes are kept is likewise named after them.

clue.text: Applying to everyone retrospectively, it's plain

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking backwards, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: on, as in a tax on something

explanation.surface: A law that applies to all people backdated, which is clear enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospectively' reverses the phrase ON ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a vast grassy plain of South America.

clue.text: Tree and snake displacing Eden's first pair

indicators.note: displacing means the snake replaces Eden's first pair of letters

explanation.surface: A tree and a serpent upsetting the first couple in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first pair' are the letters ED, which the snake displaces, while the surface hints at Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar known for its trembling leaves.

clue.text: Feeble batting failures from unsuccessful outfits

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nought by a batsman

explanation.surface: Weak cricketing performances come from teams that keep losing.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Lame ducks are firms or bodies that are failing and need help.

clue.text: Place for holiday — popular

parts.note: a spa is a resort where people holiday

explanation.surface: A destination in vogue for a summer break.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a favourite country for package-tour sunshine breaks.

clue.text: Local elite leading one state

indicators.note: leading means the word for elite comes in front of the rest

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Cal is an abbreviation of California

explanation.surface: Regional high-flyers head one US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is the medical sense: a topical ointment is applied to one area.
explanation.definitionFit: A topical treatment acts on a particular spot of the body, so it is local.

clue.text: Where a river has a rise? Just the opposite!

definitions.text: Where a river has a rise? Just the opposite!

parts.words: Where a river has a rise? Just the opposite!
parts.note: the opposite of a rise is a fall, so we need the most famous place where a river has falls

explanation.surface: A geography question about a river's source, then a twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfalls on the river between Lake Erie and Lake Ontario.

clue.text: Inhabitant of larger nest

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A creature living in a bigger nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle, a big bird that builds very large nests.

clue.text: Explorer with link to pole

parts.note: a shackle is a link or coupling

explanation.surface: An explorer connected with the Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Shackleton led Antarctic expeditions, so the surface fits the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Ernest Shackleton was a celebrated polar explorer of the Antarctic.
